query: For lightweight high-entropy alloys intended for weight-sensitive aerospace and rail-transportation applications, what single, testable intervention hypothesis could improve mechanical performance, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance while retaining low density? Specify the intervention, the proposed causal mechanism, the predicted outcomes relative to an unmodified lightweight-high-entropy-alloy baseline, the conditions under which the hypothesis should hold, the prior evidence supporting it, and a controlled experiment with clear results that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Adding Mo and optimizing the composition of lightweight high-entropy alloys can improve their mechanical performance, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance while retaining low density.
generation.material_initial_state: as-cast or wrought lightweight high-entropy alloys
generation.conditions: aerospace and rail-transportation applications, high temperatures
generation.structural_mediator: formation of hard intermetallic compounds and stable passivation film
generation.mechanism: solid-solution strengthening, formation of hard intermetallic compounds, and stable passivation film, derived from materials-science principles and records judged transfers or partially
generation.predicted_outcome: improved mechanical performance, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance
generation.boundary: limits of Mo content and composition optimization
generation.uncertainty: effects of Mo content and composition optimization on microstructure and properties

falsification_experiment.design: controlled experiment with varying Mo content and composition
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: if adding Mo and optimizing composition does not improve mechanical performance, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance, the hypothesis is falsified
